findings.evidence: Line 47-57: <div class="wizard-steps" id="s3-wizard"> contains <div class="step" id="s3-step3" style="order:3">, <div class="step" id="s3-step2" style="order:2">, <div class="step" id="s3-step1" style="order:1">. DOM sequence is step3, step2, step1; visual sequence via CSS order is step1, step2, step3.
findings.fix: Reorder child elements in DOM to match visual sequence, or remove CSS order property and reorder divs directly: step1 (order:1), step2 (order:2), step3 (order:3).
findings.violation: DOM order (step3, step2, step1) contradicts visual/CSS order (step1, step2, step3) via order property. Keyboard and screen reader users navigating DOM encounter steps in incorrect logical sequence.

findings.evidence:
Line 44-46:
. No role, aria-label, aria-button, tabindex, or onclick/keyboard handler visible.
findings.fix: Add role="button" and aria-label="Delete" (or appropriate label) to the div, and add tabindex="0" if it should receive keyboard focus. Implement keyboard handler for Enter/Space keys.
findings.violation: Div appears to be an interactive delete button (styled with class and containing icon image) but has no role="button", aria-label, tabindex, or keyboard event handler. Not exposed to assistive technology as a control.

findings.evidence: Line 64: <label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label" style="color:#cc0000">Phone number</label>. Color #cc0000 is only visual cue; input at line 65 has no required attribute or aria-required.
findings.fix: Add aria-required="true" to input #phone, or add an asterisk (*) or 'required' text after the label text.
findings.violation: Label text is colored red (#cc0000) with no asterisk, aria-required, or other non-color cue to convey that red indicates purpose or required status. Users unable to perceive color cannot identify the label's significance.
